'''Shisho Shrine''' (四所神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Fukushima|en|Fukushima|qid=Q230656|lt=Fukushima (Tokushima City)}}, {{ill|Tokushima (city)|en|Tokushima (city)|qid=Q207309|lt=Tokushima}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|qid=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture}}. It has been designated a {{ill|Q11273094|ja|とくしま市民遺産|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima Citizen Heritage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11273094}}.

== Overview ==
The origins of Shisho Shrine date back to 807 (Daido 2), according to tradition (see {{ill|Folklore|en|Folklore|qid=Q36192|lt=Legend}}). It is one of the five notable shrines of central Tokushima. 

Historically known as Shisho Myojin or Shisho Daimyojin, the shrine is affectionately called "Fukushima Myojin" by locals. 

There is a legend that a serpent resides within the shrine, though the details were nearly forgotten. Recently discovered ancient documents revealed that two sacred {{ill|Dragon Serpents|ja|龍蛇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dragon Serpents|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|en|Izumo-taisha|qid=Q696362|lt=Izumo Taisha}} are enshrined here. In 1788 (Tenmei 8), the {{ill|Dragon Serpents|ja|龍蛇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dragon Serpents|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} were delivered to the Tokushima Domain from Izumo Taisha. Revering their divine power, the domain enshrined them in Shisho Shrine, where they were venerated during ceremonial voyages. 

Two years later, in 1790 (Kansei 2), another Dragon Serpent brought by the naval commander Mori Jingobei was also enshrined. It was recorded in ''Zoku Awa Kuni Choko Zassho'' that the first serpent was male, while the second was female, forming a mystical pair.

In 2024 (Reiwa 6), the shrine began holding the {{ill|Dragon Serpent Festival|ja|龍蛇神祭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dragon Serpent Festival|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}. 

The shrine grounds include a literary monument dedicated to the novelist [[:en:Unno Juza|Unno Juza]], who grew up in the area. The shrine is also connected to {{ill|Hana Kaifu|ja|海部ハナ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hana Kaifu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11559318}}.

== Festivals ==
* {{ill|January 1|en|January 1|qid=Q2150|lt=January 1}} - New Year Festival
* {{ill|May 15|en|May 15|qid=Q2562|lt=May 15}} - Taidai Kagura Festival
* {{ill|July 8|en|July 8|qid=Q2692|lt=July 8}}, {{ill|July 9|en|July 9|qid=Q2690|lt=July 9}} - Summer Festival
* {{ill|October 27|en|October 27|qid=Q2956|lt=October 27}}, {{ill|October 28|en|October 28|qid=Q2952|lt=October 28}} - Autumn Festival (with ''Chōsa'' portable shrine)

== Legend ==
A legend recounts that in the offshore area of Tokushima City's {{ill|Q11556321|ja|津田町|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuda Town|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11556321}}, there was once an island called Kamejima, where a shrine adorned with two deer statues stood. An elderly couple visited the shrine daily until they dreamt of a deity warning, "When the deer’s eyes turn red, the island will sink; take the deer and flee." A young pRankster painted the deer’s eyes red, prompting the couple to flee with the statues. That night, a great tsunami submerged the island. Grateful for their rescue, the couple enshrined the deer at Shisho Shrine.

==Merged second translation==
'''Shisho Shrine''' (四所神社) is a Shinto shrine located in [[:en:Tokushima City|Tokushima]], {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|en|Tokushima Prefecture|qid=Q160734|lt=Tokushima Prefecture}}, Japan. It is recognized as part of the {{ill|Q11273094|ja|とくしま市民遺産|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tokushima City Heritage|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11273094}}.

== Overview ==

The origins of Shisho Shrine date back to 807 (Daido 2), according to tradition (details are provided under [[#Legend|Legend]]). It is one of the five shrines in central Tokushima.

Historically known as Shisho Myojin or Shisho Daimyojin, it remains affectionately referred to as "Fukushima's Myojin-san" by locals.

A long-standing legend mentions that "a snake resides in Shisho Shrine," though the details were nearly lost. Recently discovered historical documents reveal that two {{ill|Dragon-snake deities|ja|龍蛇神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dragon-snake deities|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} from {{ill|Izumo-taisha|en|Izumo-taisha|qid=Q696362|lt=Izumo Taisha}} are enshrined here.

In 1788 (Tenmei 8), the Tokushima Domain received a dragon-snake deity from Izumo Taisha and enshrined it in Shisho Shrine. During the domain lord's sankin-kōtai processions, the deity was carried aboard his ceremonial ship for blessings.

Two years later, in 1790 (Kansei 2), General Mori Jingoemon of the Awa Navy brought another dragon-snake deity from Izumo. The earlier deity was male, and the new one was female, forming a pair. This unusual occurrence is documented in the *Zoku Awa-koku Choko Zassho*. 

In 2024 (Reiwa 6), the Dragon-Snake Deity Festival was conducted to honor this history.

A literary monument for the novelist [[:en:Unno Juza|Unno Jūza]], a local native, stands in front of the shrine. It is also associated with {{ill|Hana Kaifu|ja|海部ハナ|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kaifu Hana|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11559318}}.

== Festivals ==

* {{ill|January 1|en|January 1|qid=Q2150|lt=January 1}} - New Year’s Festival (Saijitsusai)
* {{ill|May 15|en|May 15|qid=Q2562|lt=May 15}} - Grand Kagura Festival
* {{ill|July 8|en|July 8|qid=Q2692|lt=July 8}}–{{ill|July 9|en|July 9|qid=Q2690|lt=July 9}} - Summer Festival
* {{ill|October 27|en|October 27|qid=Q2956|lt=October 27}}–{{ill|October 28|en|October 28|qid=Q2952|lt=October 28}} - Autumn Festival (Ship Danjiri)

== Grounds ==

* '''Ten Shrine''' (天神社)
* '''Iō Shrine''' (醫王神社)
* '''Fukuro Tree''': A pine tree designated as the first municipal protected tree of Tokushima City in 1974 (Showa 49).
* A literary monument to [[:en:Unno Juza|Unno Jūza]] stands on the shrine grounds. Nearby, there are temples such as {{ill|Tōshō-ji Temple (Tokushima)|ja|東照寺 (徳島市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tōshōji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11528047}} and {{ill|Jiko-ji Temple|ja|慈光寺 (徳島市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jikōji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11494985}}.

== Legend ==

In the past, an island called Kamejima existed off the coast of {{ill|Q11556322|ja|津田町 (徳島市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tsuda Town, Tokushima City|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11556322}}. A shrine on the island featured two decorated deer. An elderly couple who visited daily dreamed that the shrine deity warned them, "If the deer’s eyes turn red, the island will sink. Take the deer and flee."

A mischievous youth painted the deer’s eyes red, prompting the couple to escape with the deer by boat. That night, a massive tsunami submerged the island. Believing their rescue was thanks to the deer, the couple enshrined them at Shisho Shrine. This story is recounted in local lore.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.topics.or.jp/nie/117307666665/121360160271.html |title=Legend of Kameiso: Deer Protect Elderly Couple from Tsunami |work=Tokushima Shimbun |date=2008-06-16 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20101017044927/https://www.topics.or.jp/nie/117307666665/121360160271.html |archivedate=2010-10-17}}</ref>

* {{ill|Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|諏訪神社 (徳島市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Suwa Shrine (Tokushima City)}} - Located in Minamisako, Tokushima
* {{ill|Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima City)|ja|八幡神社 (徳島市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hachiman Shrine (Tokushima City)}} - Located in Iga, Tokushima
* {{ill|Konpira Shrine (Tokushima)|ja|金刀比羅神社 (徳島市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrine (Tokushima City)}} - Located in Semimachi, Tokushima
